available.statement: For an abelian subvariety B of an abelian variety J over the permitted perfect ground field, there is a complementary abelian subvariety Z with finite B intersection Z and B+Z=J; the addition map B times Z→J is an isogeny.
available.hypotheses: B is an abelian subvariety over the same ground field. Choose an ample line bundle H on J over that field. The proof uses the reduced identity component of ker(J→Jdual→Bdual).
available.parameter_range: All dimensions, allowing Z=0; the current ground field has characteristic0.
available.normalizations: The map J→Jdual is phi_H and Bdual is obtained by dualizing the actual inclusion B→J.
available.limit_order: Choose the inclusion and ample H, construct Z over the same field, then prove finite intersection and the dimension inequality.

needed: For the actual B0=image(A→J) over Lprime, construct Z/Lprime such that B0 times Z→J and A times Z→J are Lprime-isogenies; hence dim J>=2.
derivation: The prior nonzero Lprime-homomorphism A→J and absolute simplicity give a finite-kernel surjection A→B0; these are incoming facts. Apply the source with ground field Lprime, which is a number field and therefore perfect. Choose H over Lprime; every morphism in J→Jdual→B0dual is over Lprime, so the reduced identity component Z is over Lprime. Restricting the map to B0 gives phi_(H restricted B0), with finite kernel because the restriction is ample. Therefore B0 intersection Z is finite. The kernel dimension gives dim Z>=dim J-dim B0, while finite intersection forces the image of B0 times Z to have dimension dim B0+dim Z<=dim J. Equality follows and the closed connected image is J. Thus addition is an isogeny. Composing with the incoming A→B0 isogeny gives the required A times Z→J over Lprime. Since A is a surface, dim J>=2. No field extension, degree bound or principal polarization on A or Z is introduced.
incoming: The same Lprime and actual nonzero A→J homomorphism from the preceding Hom theorem step.
Absolute simplicity of the original dimension-two A.
Projectivity of J supplies an ample line bundle defined over Lprime.
boundary: No effective degree bound for this preliminary isogeny, no change of ground field, and no proof of the preceding Hom or modular-Jacobian input. The later effective isogeny estimate remains separate.
